clue.text: After tax joint funds sink

parts.note: cess is an old word for a local tax or levy
a pool is money put together by several people

explanation.surface: Once the taxman has had his share, the money a group put in together goes down the drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cesspool is an underground pit that collects waste water, a kind of sump.

clue.text: Percussion instrument's character in sound reproduction

definitions.note: read as 'percussion instrument is', the 's being is

indicators.note: in sound reproduction means the word is to be reproduced as a sound, that is spoken

parts.note: a symbol is a written character or sign

explanation.surface: A drum kit's personality shows in the hi-fi recording.
explanation.definitionFit: The cymbal is a brass plate struck to make a clash in an orchestra or drum kit.

clue.text: Failure to hold up snout and this may choke

indicators.note: to hold up means in this down clue the first word sits above the second

parts.note: snout is prison slang for tobacco, something to smoke
a bomb is slang for a flop or failure

explanation.surface: Not keeping your nose up leads to choking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold up' only works as a placement signal because this is a down clue, where one piece can sit above another; 'snout' is prison slang, not a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoke bomb gives off thick fumes that can make people cough and gasp.

clue.text: Board separating throne and gracious royal adviser

indicators.note: separating means the first piece comes between the other two

parts.note: throne is slang for a lavatory, as is privy
Lor is a dated exclamation like 'goodness gracious'
a council is a governing board

explanation.surface: A committee stands between the monarch's seat and a kindly courtier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separating' places the board between the other two pieces. 'Throne' looks regal but is slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Privy Counsellor is a member of the body that formally advises the British monarch.

clue.text: Start to attend some rock music

parts.note: the off is the start of a race
to attend somewhere is to be at it

explanation.surface: Someone begins going to a few rock gigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Reggae and ska stress the weak beats of the bar, a rhythm named after the unaccented beat.

clue.text: Listless macaw spies a tree

indicators.note: a list is a cloth's border strip, so a word without its lists has lost its edges

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: A lethargic parrot keeps watch on a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listless' looks like 'lethargic', but here a list is a border, so the macaw loses its first and last letters, leaving ACA.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a thorny tree or shrub of warm countries, also called wattle.

clue.text: Sweet brew of hot cocoa Mel uses

indicators.note: a brew is a mixture made by stirring things together, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Mel makes a pudding from hot cocoa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' is the British word for a dessert course, not a single sweetie.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light whipped dessert, here flavoured with cocoa.

clue.text: I'm into film sound

indicators.note: into means the first piece is put inside the second

parts.note: Che is a 2008 film about Che Guevara

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a role in a movie soundtrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A chime is a ringing bell tone.

clue.text: A blue rag? That's surely incorrect

definitions.text: A blue rag? That's surely incorrect

indicators.note: incorrect signals that the letters of the words are not in their right order

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether a rag really is blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrect' rearranges A BLUE RAG; the whole clue shows a claim being disputed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open to dispute can be contested, as the doubtful question shows.

clue.text: Patron of Lawrence finally settled in Eastwood

indicators.note: settled in means the letter is put inside the actor's name

parts.note: Clint Eastwood is the American film actor

indicators.note: finally takes only the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: A supporter of D. H. Lawrence at last makes a home in the writer's birthplace, Eastwood.
explanation.walkthrough: D. H. Lawrence was born in Eastwood, Nottinghamshire, which makes the surface sound literary; Eastwood is really the actor Clint.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is a customer who uses a business's services.

clue.text: I wander about N.z.

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the two words are read from right to left

parts.note: to roam is to wander

explanation.surface: A traveller describes rambling around New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns I ROAM back to front. The whole clue is what a native of New Zealand might say, with 'N.z.' fixing the people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the Polynesian first people of New Zealand, so one of them roams its islands.

clue.text: Grasping fans

definitions.meaning: ... an argument means understanding or grasping it
a band's ... is its body of supporters

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is understanding a speaker; the other is a body of admirers, as a celebrity has.

clue.text: Energy in latency dissipated by last of noble gas

indicators.note: in means the first letter is placed inside the rearranged word
dissipated means scattered, so the letters of latency are spread into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Sounds like a physics lesson on how energy leaks away from a noble gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissipated' rearranges LATENCY to ACTYLEN; 'in' puts E inside it to give ACETYLEN, and 'last of' adds the final E of 'noble'. 'Noble gas' misleads: acetylene is not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetylene is a flammable hydrocarbon used in welding torches.

clue.text: Musical theatre works in Latin

definitions.meaning: drama set to music and sung on stage
the Latin word opus, a work, has this plural

explanation.definitionFit: The word names sung stage drama, and in Latin it is the plural of opus, meaning works.

clue.text: Unbeaten, on a century, back on strike

indicators.note: back means the word for a century is read in reverse

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred
workers on strike are said to be out

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the batsman is unbeaten on a hundred, and back facing the bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman who is not dismissed is unbeaten; 'on strike' is cricket talk for facing the bowling, but here it means downing tools, as striking workers do.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman who is still in at the end of an innings has not been dismissed, so remains undefeated.

clue.text: Public transport a Spice Girl finds a hindrance

parts.note: a tram is a street railway vehicle
Mel B and Mel C were both members of the pop group the Spice Girls

explanation.surface: Someone finds that taking the tram with a pop star is more nuisance than help.
explanation.definitionFit: A trammel is a restraint or impediment, originally a net or shackle.

clue.text: Mark agreed with Italian ecclesiastic

parts.note: M is short for mark, the old German currency
if a plan is on, it has been agreed
signor is the Italian for Mister, an Italian man

explanation.surface: A man called Mark makes a deal with an Italian priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A monsignor is a Roman Catholic priest given an honorary title by the Pope.

clue.text: Lefties touring ulster, maybe British soldiers

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: reds are left-wingers
an ulster is a long overcoat, an example of a coat

explanation.surface: Left-wing activists travel around Northern Ireland, perhaps meeting the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ulster' is lower case: an overcoat, not the province.
explanation.definitionFit: British infantry wore red tunics, hence the old nickname.

clue.text: Monetary system covering RBS possibly provides elevated protection

indicators.note: covering means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: EMS is the European Monetary System
the Royal Bank of Scotland is an example of a bank

explanation.surface: A financial report on a currency scheme shielding a struggling Scottish bank.
explanation.walkthrough: RBS, the Royal Bank of Scotland, was bailed out by the UK government in 2008, which colours the surface; 'covering' does the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: To embank a river is to build raised earth banks along it to hold back floods.

clue.text: Is it comical? Somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat means only some of the run of letters is taken

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a show is funny and decides it partly is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' takes a run of letters from 'Is it comical'; the whole clue describes a TV comedy that may or may not be funny.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is a television or radio series meant to make viewers laugh.

clue.text: Woman one's reviewed in The Edge of Love

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed, looked at again from the other end, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name
one is I, and the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A film critic looks at a woman's part in a romantic drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' turns ANNE IS backwards. The definition is a film credit: Sienna Miller starred in The Edge of Love (2008), about Dylan Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress Sienna Miller played Caitlin Thomas in that 2008 film.

clue.text: A party's arranged for Persian office

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A party is organised for an official in Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap governed a province of ancient Persia; a satrapy is his post or province.

clue.text: He wrote exalted English novel primarily about Tristram Shandy's origins

indicators.note: exalted means raised up, so in this down clue the letters read from bottom to top
primarily takes the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: origins takes the first letters of the two names

explanation.surface: A tribute to the author of a celebrated English novel about the origins of Tristram Shandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exalted' turns ENRETS upwards. Laurence Sterne really wrote Tristram Shandy, whose hero tells of his own birth, so the surface is true.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the eighteenth-century writer of the comic novel Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: Omnivore leaving last two bits of crust

indicators.note: leaving last two bits of means the final pair of letters of the word is dropped

parts.note: a crust is an outer coating

explanation.surface: An animal that eats anything walks off leaving the ends of a pie crust.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a raccoon-like American mammal that eats both plants and small animals.

clue.text: Bright star's best mark

definitions.meaning: the brightest star in a constellation gets the first Greek letter
a top grade for an exam or essay

explanation.definitionFit: The first Greek letter names a constellation's brightest star and a top grade.

clue.text: One scoring points for art

parts.note: read as someone marking skin with needle points to make a picture, not a player earning points

explanation.surface: A competitor earns points in an art contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A body artist pricks ink into skin with a needle to make designs.

clue.text: Looking left and right Pop almost set free American horse

indicators.note: looking left means the word for dad is read right to left, before it is read again the normal way

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
pa again, read left to right this time

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: loose means set free

explanation.surface: Dad glances both ways before nearly releasing a horse from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking left and right' gives PA twice, first backwards (AP), then forwards. 'almost' cuts LOOSE to LOOS.
explanation.definitionFit: The appaloosa is a spotted breed of horse from the American north-west.

clue.text: Hospital casualty in u.s. is more healthy

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital for convalescents
the ER, emergency room, is the American name for a casualty department

explanation.surface: A patient in an American hospital is getting better.
explanation.definitionFit: Saner is the comparative of sane, sound in mind, so healthier mentally.

clue.text: Stellar blast over railway

indicators.note: over means the exclamation is turned round

parts.note: blast and rats are both exclamations of annoyance

explanation.surface: A dazzling explosion above the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses RATS to STAR. 'blast' looks like an explosion but is a mild curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe things to do with the stars or shining like them.

clue.text: I'm amazed imprisoned pop star lost his first band

indicators.note: lost his first means the earliest of the given letter in the name is dropped

parts.note: the singer Boy George was jailed in 2009
a ring or band is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A jailed singer has lost his original group.
explanation.walkthrough: BOY GEORGE drops his first O, the ring shape 'band' stands for. 'band' looks like his group Culture Club.
explanation.definitionFit: This old-fashioned exclamation expresses surprise or astonishment.
